newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 20.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh has suggested that future governments be guaranteed a four-year term of office in the new constitution. He believes it should be impossible for governments to be voted out of power through a censure debate and the premier should also be banned from dissolving parliament. The move, he says, will improve the stability of the government and prevent them from changing so often. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Cabinet will probably review a bill to create parliamentary ombudsmen before presenting it to the House of Representatives. An informed source at the Government House says the bill is hardly a breakthrough that could effectively improve the political system. The ombudsmen would have only limited powers and their general task would be to monitor public complaints against members of parliament, senators, politicians and political appointees and make recommendations. (THE NATION)

- Changes are imminent at various key posts at the Police Department following a series of crackdowns on gambling dens in Bangkok and the provinces over the past few weeks. Rumours had it at the time that there would be swift and numerous transfers of those close to former police chief Pochana Boonyachinda, when he was removed from the top police job two months ago. (THE NATION)

- The option for relocating the second Bangkok international airport from the Nong Ngu Hao site is still under consideration pending a thorough study of the matter, says Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh. It was earlier rumoured that the second airport might be abandoned because of many problems, including cost increases. A proposal has been made to use the airport site for a flood prevention scheme instead. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Thai Airways International's safety record has come under fire from Australia, compounding problems for the airline which has already been downgraded by international media for its service quality. THAI insists its record is up to standard. (BANGKOK POST)
